# Executive summary

Instructors and learners choosing an R tutorial often have to inspect its repository to check the requirements and find evidence that the exercises still work. Lessons use different formats, and their descriptions may leave prerequisites or maintenance status unclear.

**tutorialverse will help instructors and learners find R tutorials suited to their needs, understand the prerequisites, and see when the materials were last checked and reviewed.** We will build an R package with adapters that check tutorials made with existing engines and report the results in a common format. A searchable registry will combine those reports with tutorial descriptions and human reviews. Authors will keep their lessons in their own repositories, with community review of submissions and a process for handling outdated entries.

The 12-month project will initially support learnr, learnr2, and Quarto Live, with four small example tutorials to test the adapters across teaching contexts. Carpentries-style materials will also be indexed, with stated limits on automated checks. Existing tools will provide browser execution and static hosting.
